record.original_question: Do volume preserving actions of surface groups on R2 satisfy the Milnor–Wood inequality?

evidence.quote: Question 3.18. Do volume preserving actions of surface groups on R2 satisfy the Milnor–Wood inequality?

artifact.category_tag: Surface group actions and Euler class
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_g$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \ge 2$, and let $\Gamma_g = \pi_1(\Sigma_g)$ be its fundamental group. Let $\mathrm{Diff}^{\,\omega}_{vol}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ denote the group of orientation-preserving (smooth) diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^2$ preserving the standard area form $\omega = dx \wedge dy$. For any homomorphism $\rho \colon \Gamma_g \to \mathrm{Diff}^{\,\omega}_{vol}(\mathbb{R}^2)$, one can associate an Euler number $\mathrm{eu}(\rho) \in \mathbb{Z}$ (the Euler number of the induced flat $\mathbb{R}^2$-bundle over $\Sigma_g$, defined for instance via bounded cohomology or via the rotation cocycle of the action).

Determine whether every such volume-preserving action $\rho$ of $\Gamma_g$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfies the Milnor–Wood inequality
$$|\mathrm{eu}(\rho)| \le |\chi(\Sigma_g)| = 2g - 2.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published proof or counterexample establishing the Milnor–Wood inequality for area-preserving surface group actions on the plane. The classical Milnor–Wood inequality is known for flat circle bundles and for various symmetric-space targets, and recent work has extended it in several directions, but the specific question for volume-preserving actions on $\mathbb{R}^2$ appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Milnor–Wood inequality - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Milnor–Wood inequality is an obstruction to endow circle bundles over surfaces with a flat structure.
status_evidence.claim: Standard statement of Milnor–Wood concerns flat circle bundles; no mention of resolution for area-preserving R^2 actions.

status_evidence.title: A new proof of Milnor-Wood inequality
status_evidence.snippet: A new proof of the classical Milnor–Wood inequality for flat bundles over surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to revisit classical Milnor–Wood; no result reported for volume-preserving R^2 actions.
